texts.text: הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְשָׁלוֹם וְהַעֲמִידֵנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ לְחַיִּים וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ וְתַקְּנֵנוּ בְּעֵצָה טוֹבָה מִלְּפָנֶיךָ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ וְהָגֵן בַּעֲדֵנוּ וְהָסֵר מֵעָלֵינוּ אוֹיֵב דֶּבֶר וְחֶרֶב וְרָעָב וְיָגוֹן וְהָסֵר שָׂטָן מִלְּפָנֵינוּ וּמֵאַחֲרֵינוּ וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ תַּסְתִּירֵנוּ כִּי אֵל שׁוֹמְרֵנוּ וּמַצִּילֵנוּ אָתָּה כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָתָּה וּשְׁמוֹר צֵאתֵנוּ וּבוֹאֵנוּ לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם מֵעַתָּה וְעַד עוֹלָם. וּפְרוֹשׂ עָלֵינוּ סֻכַּת שְׁלוֹמֶךָ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַפּוֹרֵשׂ סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם עָלֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל־עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלָםִ:

וְשָׁמְרוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶת־הַשַּׁבָּת לְדֹרֹתָם בְּרִית עוֹלָם: בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹת הִוא לְעֹלָם כִּי־שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְהוָה אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ:
תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֶּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ: כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב:
וְעַתָּה יִגְדַּל־נָא כֹּחַ אֲדֹנָי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ לֵאמֹר: זְכֹר רַחֲמֶיךָ יְיָ וַחֲסָדֶיךָ כִּי מֵעוֹלָם הֵמָּה:
texts.position: below English rubric, 2 indented lines, smaller type

texts.text: יִתְגַּדַּל וְיִתְקַדַּשׁ שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא בְּעָלְמָא דִּי־בְרָא כִרְעוּתֵהּ וְיַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ בְּחַיֵּיכוֹן וּבְיוֹמֵיכוֹן וּבְחַיֵּי דְכָל־בֵּית־יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּעֲגָלָא וּבִזְמַן קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן.
יְהֵא שְׁמֵהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ לְעָלַם וּלְעָלְמֵי עָלְמַיָּא.

יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיִשְׁתַּבַּח וְיִתְפָּאַר וְיִתְרוֹמַם וְיִתְנַשֵּׂא וְיִתְהַדָּר וְיִתְעַלֶּה וְיִתְהַלָּל שְׁמֵהּ דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְעֵלָּא וּלְעֵלָּא מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא וְשִׁירָתָא תֻּשְׁבְּחָתָא וְנֶחֱמָתָא דַּאֲמִירָן בְּעָלְמָא, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן:

uncertainties: Hashkiveinu final word: the vowel layout looks like יְרוּשָׁלָםִ (hiriq under final mem, no yod). Defective spelling, not confirmed at this resolution.
סֻכַּת (three times): qubbuts read under samekh. Could be a qamats-like mark at scan resolution.
Hashkiveinu line 6: the first אָתָּה is read with qamats under alef, the second also אָתָּה. The chatimah has אַתָּה with patah. The qamats readings are tentative.
Veshamru: לְדֹרֹתָם read as defective (holam, no vav). Could be לְדוֹרֹתָם.
Veshamru: אוֹת הִוא vs הִיא. The small type makes the vav/yod hard to tell apart. Recorded as הִוא, tentatively.
Veshamru prints the Tetragrammaton as יְהוָה, while Hashkiveinu, Zekhor and the chatimah print יְיָ. Recorded as printed, not normalized.
Numbers 14:17 is printed as אֲדֹנָי (fully pointed adonai), recorded as seen.
Speaker label before יתגדל is a small superscript abbreviation. It is most likely חזן, but the letters are tiny.
Kaddish: the holam vav in וְיִתְרוֹמַם is not certain (it could be וְיִתְרֹמַם). The absence of dagesh in כִרְעוּתֵהּ and דְכָל is not certain either.
Mappiq in שְׁמֵהּ / כִרְעוּתֵהּ / מַלְכוּתֵהּ is assumed from the printed dots, which are faint.
The (בשבת) rubric is in Rashi script inside parentheses and is not pointed.

headings.text: Evening Prayer for the New Year

instructions.position: start of second paragraph, before cue ושמרו
centred italic rubric after Tik'u paragraph

texts.text: Lead us to rest, O Lord our God, in peace, and let us rise, O our King, to life. Spread over us the tent of Thy peace and improve us through good counsel from before Thee. Help us for the sake of Thy Name, protect us and remove from us foe, pestilence, sword, famine and grief. Remove Satan from in front of us and behind us; and in the shadow of Thy wings shelter us, for Thou art God, our guardian and our deliverer, for Thou art God, a gracious and merciful King. Guard our going out and our return to life and peace from now to eternity. Spread over us the tent of Thy peace. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who spreads the tent of peace over us and over all His people Israel and over Jerusalem.

The Children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath to celebrate the Sabbath throughout their generations as an eternal covenant. Between Me and the Children of Israel it shall be a sign for ever, that in six days the Lord created the heavens and the earth and on the seventh day He ceased from work and rested.
Blow the Shofar on the New Moon when the moon is covered on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob.
And now let the power of the Lord appear great, as Thou hast said. Remember Thy compassion, O Lord and Thy kindnesses, for they exist since eternity.

Exalted and sanctified be His Great Name in the world which He has created according to His will. May His Kingdom be established in your lifetime and in your days and in the lifetime of the whole House of Israel, speedily and in a short time, and say: Amen!
May His Great Name be praised to eternity and the eternity of eternities!

Blessed and praised and glorified and elevated and exalted and adorned and raised on high and lauded be the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He; high, yea high, above all blessing and song, praise and comfort that have ever been spoken in the world, and say Amen!

uncertainties: 'O Lord and Thy kindnesses' has no comma after 'Lord' in the source. Recorded as printed.
'say: Amen!' (paragraph 5) has a colon but 'say Amen!' (paragraph 7) has none. Recorded as printed.

limits: I read only the two JPGs (shown downscaled to 1208x2000 from 1368x2264) at medium effort. I did not zoom in on any region, so fine pointing (dagesh, holam vs. qamats, hiriq placement, mappiq) in small type is less reliable than the consonants.

I consulted no OCR, primary reading, XML or other edition. Where pointing could not be resolved from the image, it is listed under uncertainties rather than corrected from memory. Even so, some vowels I could barely see may have been filled in by expectation; the items in the uncertainties lists are the most likely cases.
Verse identities (Exod 31:16–17, Ps 81:4–5, Num 14:17, Ps 25:6) are my identifications. They are not printed in the source.
On s24 there are no Hebrew-page cues pointing to the English. The only English on s24 is the rubric 'The Reader says half Kaddish.'
